title: Porting Rockbox to an undocumented $9 Aliexpress 'YP3' MP3 Player with LLMs

excerpt: Porting Rockbox to an undocumented $9 Aliexpress 'YP3' MP3 Player with LLMs Rockbox is a wonderful old custom firmware project for a variety of MP3 players and iPods. Flashing rockbox to my Sansa E200 was a seminal moment for me: computers were everywhere, and if they didn’t do cool things, it was because no one had bothered to program them to do so. Looking back, that played no small part in my choice of career. It seems like in 2026 there aren’t any cheap MP3 players that Rockbox supports though. Reverse engineering an embedded platform like this is one of the hardest things I can think of, and I had decided to pay the big bucks for one of those delicious subsidized token plans to try and push it as hard as I could, and I did have a dirt cheap $9 Aliexpress MP3 player lying around. TL;DR: it ported Rockbox to a 512 KiB player, I was barely involved. Then, I had it build a re-usable toolkit/set of skills for future ports based on what worked from the first attempt approach, and Claude was able to get Rockbox running on another MP3 player (TS47) in 4 hours. I made a quick website for the project: Here is the porting toolkit: auto-rockbox Enter: The YP3 This is an unbranded player, sold under a variety of fake consonant soup brands on Amazon as well as Aliexpress. You can order them wholesale from Alibaba for less than $7 or so each. It calls itself a yp3_2.0.43 in the “About” menu as. This appears to be a listing for a YP3 - the original is gone. I paid $9.71 for mine, shipped. NOTE: Before you run off and buy one, I have another rockbox port that is probably a week or two out, it is booting and stable, just needs more acceptance testing.
